jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.



The Business Marketing team contributes to our broader mission of ensuring responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence by developing and executing strategies that drive awareness, engagement, and usage for OpenAI’s products and platform amongst core business audiences.



The Strategy & Operations function helps Business Marketing turn priorities into effective programs and sound investment decisions. We work across strategic planning, portfolio and resource management, budgets, measurement, and operating systems. The team is expected to jump into a wide range of programs, stand them up, and run them for as long as needed.



About the Role

We’re looking for a resourceful program manager and Strategy & Operations generalist to help Business Marketing tackle changing priorities. Your work may span cross-functional program management, budget planning and analysis, and designing new programs from zero to one. You’ll step into unfamiliar problems, build the structure needed to make progress, and stay hands-on through launch and ongoing operations.



You’ll partner with marketing leaders, Finance, Creative Operations, and other teams to shape programs, organize and lead working teams, and clarify ownership. You’ll help leaders weigh investment decisions and trade-offs, connecting business goals with the budget, capacity, and effort required to deliver.



This role combines strong financial knowledge and practical judgment with hands-on program management and a builder’s instinct. You should enjoy making sense of ambiguity, learning unfamiliar areas quickly, and figuring out how much structure a problem needs. Alongside standing up and running programs, you’ll help manage our portfolio and build AI-enabled workflows that make work easier across the department.



This is a hybrid role, based on our San Francisco office three days a week.



In this role, you will:

 - Stand up and run cross-functional programs. Take varied initiatives from initial definition through launch and ongoing operations. Coordinate dependencies, resolve blockers, adapt scope as priorities evolve, and remain accountable for running the program for as long as needed. When a transition makes sense, establish a clear owner and effective handoff.

 - Manage the portfolio and resource trade-offs. Maintain a clear view of active and upcoming work, team responsibilities, and available capacity. Help leaders prioritize work against business goals, identify dependencies and constraints, and choose where to invest time and resources.

 - Design new programs from zero to one. Clarify the problem, audience, business objective, scope, and measures of success. Turn incomplete requests into actionable briefs and practical operating models. Decide whether work belongs in an existing program, needs a new approach, or can be handled through self-service, and test and refine the solution as you learn.

 - Organize and lead effective working teams. Establish accountable owners, decision rights, milestones, working rhythms, and shared information. Keep stakeholders aligned and help teams make decisions and follow through. Partner with Creative Operations on staffing, capacity, agency needs, and production timelines when the program calls for it.

 - Support budgets and investment decisions. Partner with Finance and program owners on budget planning, tracking, and analysis. Develop clear views of costs, assumptions, expected value, and resource needs. Evaluate scenarios and explain financial and operational trade-offs so leaders can make informed investment decisions.

 - Build useful systems and AI-enabled workflows. Improve intake, portfolio visibility, and the shared information teams rely on. Use OpenAI products, automation, team feedback, and delivery patterns to simplify processes and reduce repetitive coordination. Build and refine solutions that people adopt and that remain useful as the business grows.



You might thrive in this role, if you have:

 - 7+ years of experience in strategy and operations, business operations, program or project management, or related work across multiple teams and concurrent priorities.

 - A track record of personally organizing and leading cross-functional teams, establishing ownership, managing dependencies, and taking programs from initial design through delivery and sustained operations.

 - Strong financial knowledge, including experience with budget planning, tracking, and analysis. You can assess costs, assumptions, expected value, and resource constraints to support investment decisions and explain trade-offs clearly.

 - Strong judgment in ambiguous situations, including the ability to distinguish urgency from importance, ask the right questions, and make practical recommendations with incomplete information.

 - Experience building programs and operating models from zero to one, including intake processes, project structures, and portfolio systems that people adopt because they make work easier.

 - Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools, automations, or workflows, with concrete examples of how they improved work. You can move from identifying a problem to testing and implementing a useful solution.

 - The ability to build trust with marketing leaders, Finance, creatives, and operational partners, including when you need to challenge an ask, align competing priorities, or recommend a different path.

 - A generalist’s approach to problem-solving: curiosity, structured thinking, comfort with unfamiliar problems, and a willingness to jump into different programs and do the hands-on work for as long as needed.

 - A bias toward simplicity and sustainable execution. You create clarity and momentum without adding meetings, process, or maintenance that outweigh their value.

jobs.title: Safety Response Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

At OpenAI, our Trust, Safety & Risk Operations teams safeguard our products, users, and the company from abuse, fraud, scams, regulatory non-compliance, and other emerging risks. We operate at the intersection of operations, compliance, user trust, and safety working closely with Legal, Policy, Engineering, Product, Go-To-Market, and external partners to ensure our platforms are safe, compliant, and trusted by a diverse, global user base.

The Global Safety Response Operations team provides 24/7 coverage for user safety, risk, and regulatory escalations across OpenAI’s products, handling the highest-priority cases that require human judgment and rapid response. The team operates as the core escalation and delivery arm of OpenAI’s safety operations, ensuring that our products remain safe and aligned with policy while enabling timely, empathetic, and consistent user support.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Global Safety Response Operations Lead is a hands-on team lead who both manages a regional Safety Response team and personally handles high-risk safety cases. This role combines frontline safety work with people leadership, operational ownership, and cross-functional coordination.

You will lead a team of Safety Response Analysts who handle OpenAI’s most sensitive and high-impact cases, while also personally contributing to casework for complex, high-risk, or high-visibility issues.  You will own the execution of high severity escalations in your region and ensure proper execution and communication to cross functional stakeholders

You will be accountable for ensuring your region consistently meets utilization, quality, and SLA targets while serving as the operational interface with Product, Policy, Legal, Investigations, and regional stakeholders.

This is a 24/7 global operation that requires flexibility to support rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, and holidays, as part of a leadership on-call model.



In This Role, You Will:

 - Lead and coach a regional team of Safety Response Analysts, ensuring high performance, engagement, and consistent decision quality.

 - Own regional operational outcomes, including utilization, SLA adherence, backlog health, and quality benchmarks.

 - Handle and oversee the most complex and high-risk cases, serving as the first line of escalation and incident lead for your region.

 - Contribute directly to frontline work (20–30%), including investigations, enforcement decisions, and regulatory or legal escalations.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Product, Policy, Legal, Investigations, and local market teams to execute safety outcomes and manage risk.

 - Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement, improving workflows, tools, automation, and escalation paths.

 - Identify emerging risks and trends, translating frontline insights into actionable recommendations for policy, product, or enforcement.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - You have 8+ years of experience in Trust & Safety, Risk Operations, Investigations, Fraud, Annotation, or platform integrity.

 - You have 4+ years of direct people leadership or senior-level operational ownership, including coaching experienced operators, setting clear direction and supporting independent judgement.

 - You have applied AI tools and automation to improve operational workflows, with sound judgment about where human review remains essential.

 - You are deeply familiar with trust and safety operations, across multiple risk areas including content moderation, user safety, fraud, or developer risk frameworks, including the legal, policy, and technical considerations that shape enforcement.

 - You are a strong decision-maker in ambiguous, high-risk environments, able to balance speed, accuracy, and defensibility when handling sensitive or high-impact cases.

 - You communicate complex safety and risk decisions clearly and credibly, whether writing escalation narratives, briefing Legal or Policy, or aligning Product and leadership during incidents.

 - You can translate between frontline operations and strategic stakeholders, turning messy real-world cases into structured insights and turning policy or product direction into clear, executable guidance for your team.

 - You are skilled at influencing without authority, building trust with Product, Policy, Legal, Investigations, and regional partners to drive alignment and resolve ambiguity.

 - You use data, tooling, and automation to improve quality, efficiency, and scale to not just measure performance, but to make better decisions.

 - You are comfortable leading in a 24/7, high-pressure operational environment, providing calm, credible leadership during incidents, spikes, and regulatory or reputational events.

OpenAI for Government helps public-sector institutions use advanced AI responsibly to improve services and advance critical missions. The Partnerships team builds the external ecosystem and internal operating mechanisms required to deliver that work at scale.



Role Summary

We are seeking a Partnerships Operations Lead to build and run the operating foundation for OpenAI for Government’s Partnerships team.

This person will serve as the operational connective tissue across the partner team, working closely with Account Directors, Solutions Architects, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and other cross-functional stakeholders to move opportunities from initial engagement through agreement and execution.

They will help ensure a smooth handoff to Technical Success across accounts by establishing clear readiness criteria, capturing the right commercial and customer context, and aligning teams on partner roles, commitments, dependencies, and success outcomes.

The ideal candidate is a true utility player who combines the relationship instincts of a growth oriented builder with the rigor of an exceptional business operator. They thrive in ambiguity, create processes that do not yet exist, and move fluidly between deal execution, workflow design, analysis, and cross-functional coordination.

 - Own the end-to-end operating cadence for partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, from intake and qualification through approvals, contracting, launch, and expansion.

 - Own the government-partner operating cadences for deal execution, launch tracking, and business reviews; coordinate with Revenue Operations on pipeline and forecasting inputs and turn the resulting data into concise insights and actions.

 - Identify and implement workflow, tooling, and automation improvements that reduce cycle time, eliminate recurring friction, and enable the partner team to scale.

 - A track record of building operating processes and cross-functional workflows from the ground up in a fast-moving organization.

 - Experience supporting the end-to-end deal lifecycle in enterprise technology, public sector, or another complex and regulated environment.

 - Exceptional program-management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple high-priority workstreams, stakeholders, decisions, and deadlines.

 - Strong systems and data orientation, including experience with CRM, reporting, workflow, and collaboration tools.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, sound judgment, and the ability to influence cross-functional teams without relying on formal authority.

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.

About the Role

The SMB Innovation Sales & Strategy Lead will identify, incubate and scale new revenue opportunities across OpenAI’s SMB Ads business. This foundational role combines strategic thinking, analytical rigor and hands-on execution to develop differentiated customer propositions, validate product opportunities and launch new go-to-market programs.

Working across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Data Science, this person will lead initiatives from opportunity assessment through customer discovery, commercial pilots and transition to scale. The remit includes industry-specific opportunities, differentiated customer engagement models and innovative approaches across self-serve, sales-assisted and partner-led channels.

 - Identify untapped opportunities across SMB segments, industries, and channels. Build business cases and launch pilots to validate customer demand and commercial potential.

 - Design new acquisition, activation, and expansion programs, including industry-specific and assisted-growth approaches. Partner with sales teams and outsourced sales providers to connect self-serve adoption with sales-assisted engagement.

As Head of Finance - Data Centers, you will be the finance leader for OpenAI’s self-built data center efforts. You will partner with teams across infrastructure, real estate, energy, construction, procurement, and finance to turn proposed sites into sound investment decisions and funded projects.

This role spans the full development lifecycle: evaluating opportunities, building investment cases, forecasting capital needs, managing construction budgets, and helping determine how projects should be financed. You will give leadership a clear view of project economics, funding requirements, and risks as we build data center capacity at scale.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead financial evaluation of proposed data center and related power infrastructure projects, including site economics, development costs, capacity phasing, lifecycle costs, and key risks.

 - Build and own project-level models and capital expenditure forecasts that connect construction schedules, power delivery, equipment procurement, contingencies, and funding needs.

 - Partner with development, engineering, energy, construction, and procurement leaders on decisions that affect cost, timing, and long-term performance.

 - Work with Treasury, Corporate Finance, Tax, and Legal to evaluate financing options, including project or construction debt, leases, joint ventures, and other partnership structures where appropriate.

 - Prepare investment recommendations and capital approval materials for senior leadership, translating complex project details into clear choices and tradeoffs.

 - Build a consistent portfolio view of project costs, cash requirements, milestones, and financial performance. Partner with Accounting and operations teams through project completion and handoff.

 - Prior experience as the finance leader for large-scale data center builds or major electric generation projects. You have directly owned investment analysis, capital budgets, and financial decisions through development and construction.

 - 10+ years of experience across strategic finance, infrastructure finance, project development, or related fields.

jobs.description:
About the Team

The Frontier Assurance team brings independent scrutiny into OpenAI’s safety decisions and helps the public understand and assess our safety work. We lead third-party assessments and safeguard testing for OpenAI’s flagship launches, pilot new assurance mechanisms such as embedded auditing, run our misalignment disclosure process, and incorporate independent expert input as evidence for critical safety decisions.

About the Role

As a Research Program Manager on the Frontier Assurance team, you will build programs that bring independent expertise into frontier AI safety decisions and make the evidence behind those decisions understandable to the public. You will lead external research partnerships and third-party assessments, coordinate public safety documentation, and develop new approaches to independent scrutiny and transparency. Working across research, engineering, product, policy, and communications, you will help ensure external findings inform concrete decisions and that our public explanations accurately reflect the evidence, limitations, and remaining uncertainty.

We’re looking for people with deep experience in research partnerships and program management with technical and research teams. This role combines partnership management, cross-functional coordination, an understanding of AI safety research, alignment, and evaluations, and strong communication skills. You will work with researchers and engineers within OpenAI and across the external community to initiate projects, set ambitious goals and milestones, and drive execution across multiple teams.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and run third-party assessment programs for frontier models and safeguards, including independent evaluations, adversarial testing, and new approaches such as embedded auditing. Work with researchers and external partners to define assessment questions, scope, access, timelines, and deliverables.

 - Build and manage strategic research partnerships with third-party evaluators, academic labs, and other independent experts, prioritizing expertise, independence, and diversity of perspectives. Enable rigorous research, including work that challenges internal assumptions.

 - Bring external findings to safety decision-makers and translate them into actionable recommendations for safeguards, deployment, product, and policy. Track follow-up actions and ensure partners understand how their input was considered.

 - Partner with research, product, policy, and communications teams to explain the evidence behind OpenAI’s safety approach: what we tested, what we learned, how findings shaped safeguards and deployment decisions, and where limitations and uncertainty remain. Translate complex technical results into accurate, accessible communication for expert and public audiences.

 - Lead public transparency programs, including system cards, summaries of third-party assessments, and updates on significant findings and follow-up actions. Develop approaches to sharing methods, results, and limitations while protecting privacy, security, and sensitive information.

 - Create channels for researchers and civil society to ask questions, provide feedback, and inform future assessments and transparency efforts, including beyond individual launches.

 - Own program goals, milestones, dependencies, and risks across assessment and transparency work, keeping internal and external stakeholders informed and resolving obstacles to execution.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have an understanding of AI evaluations and measurement, and can engage with technical teams on evaluation design and results.

 - Can interpret evaluation findings and communicate what they do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and disagreement.

 - Have experience building research partnerships and managing external stakeholders, especially academic researchers and independent experts.

 - Can synthesize technical and social science research into clear executive summaries and accessible explanations for public audiences.

 - Have experience delivering technical publications or public reports across multiple contributors, and exercising judgment about what to share, with whom, and when.

OpenAI’s Strategic Finance organization provides financial insights and guidance to support the company’s long-term strategy and ambitious growth. We partner across Product, Partnerships, Engineering, and GTM to allocate resources to the highest-impact opportunities while protecting sustainable unit economics.

The Applications Technology Strategic Finance team partners closely with Product to scale core offerings and bring new products to market. We lead revenue forecasting and performance management across the product portfolio, including economic margins, pricing, and partnership deal pricing and structuring.

About the Role

We are hiring a senior strategic finance thought partner to support OpenAI’s Ads business. You will partner closely with Ad Sales leadership and be responsible for driving financial planning and forecasting, evaluating new initiatives, and providing decision-quality insights on performance.

You will help build the financial foundations required to scale the Ads business—from forecasting and performance measurement to supporting our GTM strategy to economic modeling for new products and initiatives. This is a unique opportunity to influence the trajectory of frontier AI products while working at the intersection of strategy, finance, and technology.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Serve as the Strategic Finance partner to our Ads sales team, helping shape business strategy and investment decisions.

 - Support financial evaluation for our Ads business, including modeling revenue, establishing core metrics, identifying leading indicators, tracking variance to expectations, and surfacing risks and opportunities.

 - Partner with Product and GTM leaders on strategic initiatives and new product launches to shape growth plans.

 - Analyze business trends and translate data into actionable insights that inform both long-term strategy and day-to-day decision making.

 - Build and scale financial planning rigor, including forecasting methodology, management reporting, and performance narratives that improve decision velocity and accountability.

 - Stay up to date on market trends and competitive dynamics to refine financial strategies.

 - Prepare and deliver high-quality executive and Board materials communicating business performance, key drivers, and strategic recommendations.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in investment banking, consulting, or buy-side investing, coupled with operating experience at a fast-paced, scaling technology company.

 - 2+ years in Ads Finance, with Ads P&L ownership and experience supporting growth across multiple verticals, formats, and international markets.

 - Exceptional analytical and financial modeling skills, including building detailed operating models and product P&Ls to evaluate growth opportunities and investment decisions.

 - Strong business judgment and the ability to critically assess financial performance, opportunities, and risks.

 - The ability to translate complex financial data into clear insights and recommendations, and communicate them effectively to senior leadership.

 - High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy in financial analysis and reporting.

 - Familiarity with digital advertising business models.

 - A hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves mentality and comfort operating in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

 - Enthusiasm for the deployment of AI and OpenAI’s mission.

 - Experience with SQL.

jobs.title: M&A Finance Integration Lead
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.

The Finance Program Management Office (FinPMO) is responsible for driving and scaling cross-functional finance programs and M&A integrations. FinPMO partners closely across Accounting, Strategic Finance, Corporate Development, Equity, Procurement, Treasury, Risk, and Legal to ensure financial change through M&A and other new business models is executed in a controlled, auditable, and operationally effective way.

FinPMO plays a critical role in managing M&A including financial deal diligence, finance operations, post-close integrations, reporting and controls. We help quarterback the M&A process to help ensure corporate integrations are executed cleanly, risks are managed proactively, and leadership has clear deal visibility. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a M&A Finance Integration Lead, you will own and scale OpenAI’s finance integration model. This is a highly cross-functional, transactions driven role for someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, translate deal complexity into executable workplans, and drive successful M&A outcomes across multiple teams.

We’re looking for someone to be the central point of accountability to oversee finance workstreams across the full M&A lifecycle. You’ll ensure integrations are executed cleanly, financial risks are mitigated early, and our books, controls, and systems remain stable as OpenAI scales.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 


IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL:

 - Define and build standardized, scalable M&A finance integration frameworks.

 - Drive consistent execution across multiple, simultaneous M&A integrations.

 - Ensure timely, accurate M&A diligence including historical financials, revenue, equity, tax, and procurement.

 - Lead integration planning for deal close readiness across accounting, valuation, payroll, banking, entities, and controls.

 - Translate deal terms and integration strategy into actionable workplans, timelines, and dependencies.

 - Ensure on track deal execution accounting, operational integration, systems cutover, and reporting.

 - Proactively surface post-close deal integration risks and drive mitigation plans.

 


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 10+ years of experience across M&A, deal integration and finance transformation, ideally in an Investment Banking/PE backed environment and/or high-growth technology company.

 - Demonstrated experience leading multiple, concurrent M&A negotiations and deal integrations with complex cross-functional dependencies.

 - Strong understanding of deal accounting, controls and reporting in a fast changing environment.

 - Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication skills.

jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI builds powerful AI systems like ChatGPT, the OpenAI API, and enterprise products that serve millions of users across the globe. As we scale, securing our infrastructure, protecting sensitive data, supporting employees’ velocity, and meeting global compliance standards are essential to our success and societal impact.

Security at OpenAI is a cross-cutting organization that includes Security, Privacy, IT, GRC, Corporate Security, and other teams. Program Managers play a critical role in aligning teams and delivering execution at scale.



About the Role

We’re seeking a Program Manager to build and own programs that span OpenAI’s Security organization, with a core focus on Mergers & Acquisitions. You will work across domains from diligence through Day 1 readiness, integration, onboarding, and transition to ongoing ownership. You will also apply what you build to other priorities that span Security teams.  You will learn how work actually moves between teams, spot gaps and unclear ownership, and build practical systems that make complex transitions easier to execute.

This role is deeply cross-functional and execution-focused. It requires a structured operator who thrives in ambiguity, partners effectively across boundaries, and applies principled judgment to drive programs at speed from initial planning through durable handoff. You will use AI and automation to reduce repetitive work and help teams operate at greater scale, while applying sound judgment to sensitive information and consequential decisions.



In this role, you will:

 - Own Security & IT M&A programs, including supporting System Operations and other engineering teams in defining and performing timely diligence assessments, and scoping, planning, and executing acquisition integrations.  Carry the work through Day 1 readiness, onboarding of people and systems, post-close priorities, and handoff to ongoing owners.

 - Partner with Corporate Development, IT, Infrastructure, Application, Legal, Privacy, Security, GRC, Corporate Security and other teams to understand cross-functional requirements and navigate tradeoffs. Make responsibilities and decision rights clear while bringing in the right experts for technical and risk judgments.

 - Learn partner teams’ workflows and identify missed dependencies, bottlenecks, duplicated effort, and risks that could slow an integration or weaken its outcome. Address recurring problems at their source.

 - Establish scalable frameworks and processes to support core programs, including defining durable program goals and core measures of success. Build useful intake paths, playbooks, onboarding checklists, decision points, and handoff standards that teams adopt in practice.

 - Use AI and automation to organize information, surface gaps, improve documentation, route work, and track follow-through, with appropriate handling of sensitive information and human review of risk decisions.

 - Create and maintain program-level visibility across deals, risks, milestones, and dependencies, ensuring program outcomes are delivered reliably and at high quality. Measure whether the work improves readiness, reduces manual effort, closes risks, and makes future transitions more predictable.

 - Communicate status, risks, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly to technical and executive audiences and drive cross-functional execution with urgency and care.

 - Own additional programs that span Security and IT as organizational priorities evolve, applying and improving the systems built through the M&A portfolio.

 - Are an empathetic communicator and leader who is able to influence a variety of cross-functional and executive audiences, and build durable trust with partners.

 - Have carried programs from an ambiguous starting point through execution and lasting ownership.

 - Have built a new program, workflow, or operating model yourself and can show how you earned adoption and improved results.

 - Are curious about how teams work in practice and can find the underlying issue behind a missed handoff or recurring exception.

 - Have used AI or automation to improve a real workflow and can explain what changed, how people adopted it, and where human judgment remains necessary.

 - Have experience in Mergers & Acquisitions or related areas.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Government Trusted Access
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI for Government works with U.S. and allied government institutions to support the responsible adoption of AI across defense, intelligence, federal civilian, state and local, and international public-sector missions. We help public servants use frontier AI in ways that are effective, trusted, and grounded in real-world requirements for safety, reliability, security, compliance, and accountability.



Government Trusted Access programs help eligible public-sector organizations and practitioners use advanced capabilities for approved, high-value work in sensitive domains. These programs bring together OpenAI for Government, Product Policy, Legal, Security, International, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts. Each program has distinct eligibility criteria, safeguards, and decision owners; our job is to make the overall government experience coherent and executable.



About the Role

We are seeking a Program Manager to coordinate OpenAI’s Government Trusted Access portfolio across high-trust domains, such as cyber and bio. You will build and run the operating mechanisms that move government participants from initial interest through review, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, and program improvement.



The right person is a highly organized, low-ego operator who can move between strategy and detail. You are comfortable working across technical, policy, legal, safety, security, customer, and operational teams; you build durable systems without adding unnecessary process; and you communicate clearly when facts, ownership, or requirements are still evolving.



This role is based in Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will:

 - Coordinate government participation across domain-specific Trusted Access programs, including cyber and biology, while helping stand up future programs as the portfolio evolves.

 - Own the end-to-end program operating rhythm across intake, qualification, review, approval, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, renewal, and offboarding.

 - Maintain a clear portfolio view of applicants and participating organizations, access levels, requirements, owners, dependencies, commitments, risks, and decisions needed.

 - Build practical program mechanisms such as roadmaps, ownership maps, decision logs, risk registers, service standards, operating reviews, dashboards, and executive updates.

 - Coordinate cross-functional reviews across OpenAI for Government, Safety, Product Policy, Legal, Security, Product, Research, User Operations, Technical Success, Global Affairs, and domain experts.

 - Preserve clear decision boundaries: ensure the right domain owner makes eligibility, policy, safety, security, and access decisions while keeping the broader process moving.

 - Identify stalled reviews, broken handoffs, unclear ownership, capacity constraints, and recurring operational gaps; bring the right context, options, and recommendation to resolve them.

 - Partner with government-facing teams to set accurate expectations, coordinate participant communications, and ensure commitments are tracked through completion.

 - Define and monitor program health through measures such as review time, backlog age, onboarding completion, activation, support demand, participant outcomes, and operational risk.

 - Turn manual and one-off work into scalable workflows, documentation, training, automation, and tooling while retaining appropriate human judgment for sensitive decisions.

 - Capture lessons across domains and translate them into reusable operating patterns without flattening meaningful differences between programs.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Hold an active TS clearance

 - Have 5–10 years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, trust and safety, risk operations, support operations, government technology, implementation, or a related field.

 - Have led complex, cross-functional programs from an ambiguous problem statement through launch and steady-state operation.

 - Can build trust and drive alignment without direct authority while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.

 - Can translate technical, policy, legal, safety, security, and customer requirements into practical workflows and decision structures.

 - Are analytically fluent and comfortable using operational data, dashboards, case-management systems, and lightweight automation to identify bottlenecks and improve program health.

 - Communicate clearly and directly with technical teams, operators, government stakeholders, and executives, especially when evidence is incomplete or tradeoffs are sensitive.

 - Learn unfamiliar domains quickly, ask strong questions, and know when to bring in specialists rather than overstate your own expertise.

 - Operate calmly in a fast-moving environment, exercise sound judgment with sensitive information, and follow through reliably on details and commitments.

 - Experience supporting government, public-sector, national-security, regulated, or other security-conscious organizations.

jobs.title: Pricing Operations Lead
jobs.description:
About the Team

The Pricing & Monetization team is responsible for how our products create and capture value. We partner closely with Product, GTM, Finance, and Systems teams to design pricing models, packaging, and commercial strategies that support adoption, growth, and long-term scaling of the business.

To thrive in this team, you need to be a proactive problem-solver who excels at bringing structure to ambiguous challenges. Our work demands strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and precision in execution. Team members succeed when they are analytical, detail-oriented, skilled at balancing multiple priorities, and passionate about driving high-stakes projects forward to deliver meaningful results.

About the Role

We are looking for a Pricing Operations Lead to help translate pricing and packaging decisions into clear, scalable execution. You will work closely with pricing leaders and cross-functional partners across Product, Engineering, Billing, Finance, and GTM to ensure pricing changes are implemented accurately, system requirements are well managed, and launch decisions move from strategy to reality with discipline.

You should be comfortable operating at the intersection of business judgment, systems thinking, and program management. This role will help shape the operating backbone for pricing implementation, support teams developing billing and related monetization systems, and ensure the pricing team's needs are represented clearly in cross-functional planning and execution.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead the operational execution of pricing and packaging decisions from approval through implementation and launch

 - Translate pricing strategy, policies, and launch decisions into clear business requirements for billing, quoting, revenue, and related systems teams

 - Partner with Product, Engineering, Billing, Finance, and GTM teams to manage dependencies, scope tradeoffs, testing needs, and launch readiness

 - Own pricing-related requirement intake and prioritization on behalf of the pricing team, ensuring requests are clear, well managed, and tied to business needs

 - Support the design and implementation of new product, SKU, packaging, and billing configurations as pricing changes move into production

 - Establish lightweight but effective pricing operations processes, including governance, documentation, sign-offs, and issue tracking

 - Identify recurring friction in pricing execution and drive improvements that reduce ambiguity, delays, and rework

 - Have 6+ years of experience leading pricing operations or closely related monetization, commercialization, or revenue operations work

 - Have a strong track record of helping implement complex pricing or packaging decisions across cross-functional teams

 - Can translate pricing intent into practical system requirements, launch plans, operating workflows, and stakeholder decisions

 - Have experience partnering closely with billing systems, product, engineering, finance, and go-to-market teams

 - Are highly organized and comfortable managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, risks, and timelines at once

 - Communicate clearly with both business and technical audiences, and can drive accountability without creating unnecessary process

jobs.title: Strategy and Operations, OpenAI for Government
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise in custom configurations) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety.

As part of the OpenAI for Government team you will work across governments and public institutions, helping to accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored training, and early insights—so civil servants can spend less time on red tape and more on meaningful work. If you're passionate about responsibly deploying frontier AI to uplift public institutions and transform how the government serves the American people, we want you on our team.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced strategy and business operations professional to help OpenAI for Government decide where to grow and how to build the capabilities needed to serve government customers. You will shepherd ambiguous, complex work from problem definition through execution.  The majority of the role will focus on business strategy and operations, from market and revenue planning to workforce, financial, and secure facility initiatives. You should be skilled at both developing a compelling recommendation and doing the detailed work to make it happen.

This role has four key buckets of responsibilities:

 - First, you will support the growth and maturation of a business operations and revenue strategy function within the OpenAI for Government. You will help OpenAI for Government four vertical leaders develop annual business strategies that define target customers, priority projects, partners, and support needed from other matrixed teams including Technical Success, Engineering, Capture and Proposal, Global Affairs, and Product Policy.

 - You will build and maintain the intelligence picture for our key territories: mission priorities, budget lines and program timelines, incumbents and competitive positions, and the people who actually shape awards.

 - You will act as a thought partner to the business verticals by participating in weekly team discussions to understand the business, test assumptions, and identify risks. You will run quarterly reviews to track progress, reassess goals, and adjust priorities.

 - Second, you will partner with OpenAI’s industrial security team to forecast secure-space needs, plan SCIF buildouts, coordinate personnel access nominations, and track contract-specific security requirements and restrictions.

 - Third, you will support OpenAI’s Government Innovation Network, OpenAI for Government’s advisory board, throughout the entire lifecycle of the program, including advisor outreach and selection, independent-contractor agreements (1099s), conflict reviews, payment, and high-touch onboarding.

 - In partnership with OpenAI for Government’s leadership team, you will help design and run regular advisor meetings, quarterly strategy sessions, and targeted convenings, with clear agendas, materials, and decisions.  You will execute follow-through, and ensure advisor insights are integrated into OpenAI for Government’s strategy.

 - Finally, you will own and drive special projects that do not yet have a clear home. You will define the problem, develop options, build consensus, and lead early execution.
   
   


YOU’LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have experience in strategy consulting, business operations, a growing technology company, or comparable work combining analytical problem-solving with ownership of execution.

 - Can build financial models, size markets, assess competitive positions, and translate incomplete data into recommendations with clear assumptions and tradeoffs. Are comfortable interpreting government budgets and using market intelligence sources such as Janes to inform long-term investment decisions.

 - Create compelling executive presentations and write concise memos that connect the numbers, strategic choices, and recommended actions.

 - Can define an unfamiliar problem before solving it, learn new technologies and markets quickly, and make progress without a fully formed brief.

 - Enjoy a broad remit and move comfortably between strategic analysis, business operations, and detailed project delivery.

 - Build trust with executives, government stakeholders, advisors, and technical specialists, and influence across functions without formal authority.

 - Bring strong judgment and discretion to sensitive relationships, personnel matters, compensation, and security-related work.

 - Are comfortable managing budgets, vendors, contractors, and competing deadlines, and take responsibility for carrying work through to completion.

 - Are curious about government missions, procurement, policy, and funding. Direct public-sector, defense, or national-security experience is valuable, alongside strong business and analytical skills.

 - Are willing to travel periodically for advisor convenings, agency or customer engagements, and operational projects.

 - Care deeply about the mission and want to help build a durable government business grounded in the responsible deployment of frontier AI.

jobs.title: Hardware Strategic Sourcing Manager, Optics
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team builds next-generation AI-native silicon and systems while working closely with software, research, and manufacturing partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering systems for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team develops the tools, methodologies, and strategic partnerships needed to accelerate hardware innovation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re seeking an experienced Hardware Strategic Sourcing Manager to own sourcing strategy and supplier partnerships for fiber and optical interconnect components across OpenAI’s next-generation AI infrastructure.

Reporting to the Head of Partnerships & Strategic Sourcing, you will lead sourcing across fiber cable assemblies, internal optical harnesses, fiber shuffles, optical backplane assemblies, connectorized and standalone passive optical assemblies, fiber-array units (FAUs), fiber-to-chip and coupling interfaces, detachable connectors, optical routing, and assigned optical packaging, assembly, and test services.

You will work closely with electrical engineering, optical engineering, systems engineering, mechanical and packaging engineering, quality, rack integration, data-center deployment,manufacturing, supply chain, finance, legal, and program management teams to translate demanding bandwidth, signal integrity, reliability, and scale requirements into resilient supplier partnerships and scalable commercial strategies.

Your work will directly support the performance, reliability, manufacturability, and scale of the high-speed optical connectivity required for OpenAI’s next-generation AI systems.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Develop and execute a comprehensive sourcing strategy for fiber and optical interconnect components supporting high-bandwidth AI systems and infrastructure.

 - Own sourcing across optical fiber cable assemblies, internal optical harnesses, fiber shuffles, optical backplane assemblies, standalone passive optical assemblies, FAUs, fiber-to-chip interfaces, detachable connectors, and optical routingDevelop a deep understanding of the optical supply chain, including critical raw materials, fiber and cable manufacturing, connector ecosystems, component manufacturing, assembly and test capacity, and key sub-tier dependencies.

 - Identify, evaluate, qualify, and manage suppliers across the fiber and optical interconnect ecosystem, including fiber manufacturers, cable and assembly suppliers, connector manufacturers, optical component suppliers,  fiber suppliers, connector/ferrule suppliers, FAU suppliers,manufacturing partners.

 - Lead RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs; establish evaluation criteria; coordinate technical and commercial assessments; and recommend sourcing decisions aligned with performance, cost, supply security, quality, capacity, and scalability requirements.

 - Partner with engineering teams to evaluate supplier capabilities across optical performance, insertion loss, return loss, signal integrity, bandwidth, power consumption, reliability, thermal performance, mechanical robustness, manufacturability, and production readiness.

 - Partner with engineering to understand technology roadmaps and translate next-generation system requirements into sourcing strategies, supplier development plans, and long-term capacity requirements.

 - Negotiate supplier agreements covering pricing, engineering support, nonrecurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing and test capacity, lead times, quality requirements, intellectual property, warranties, service levels, and long-term supply commitments.

 - Develop and maintain detailed cost models and pricing frameworks covering fiber, connectors, cable and assembly content, optical and electronic components, manufacturing, testing, yield, logistics, supplier margins, and total cost of ownership.

 - Drive competitive cost structures through should-cost analysis, open-book pricing, benchmarking, volume agreements, value engineering, supplier competition, and multiyear cost-reduction roadmaps.

 - Collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to support supplier qualification, design reviews, component selection, validation, pilot builds, system bring-up, production readiness, and ramp to volume.

 - Establish sourcing and capacity strategies that address long lead times, constrained manufacturing capacity, sub-tier dependencies, supplier concentration, geographic and geopolitical exposure, technology transitions, and component lifecycle risks.

 - Develop multi-source and supply-continuity strategies for critical optical components, identifying where supplier concentration or specialized manufacturing capabilities create risk to development or production ramps.

 - Work with suppliers to secure capacity ahead of demand, including visibility into raw materials, manufacturing equipment, assembly capacity, test capacity, yield, and sub-tier constraints that could limit system production.

 - Build and manage strategic supplier relationships through executive engagement, business reviews, performance scorecards, issue escalation, corrective action plans, and alignment on future fiber and optical-interconnect technology roadmaps.

 - Partner with finance, legal, security, quality, and operations teams to ensure sourcing decisions meet technical, commercial, compliance, and risk-management requirements.

 - Develop repeatable processes and reporting for category strategy, supplier performance, pricing, capacity planning, component availability, and supply risk, including relevant ERP, MRP, and PLM workflows.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - Ten or more years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supplier management, or supply-chain leadership within optical communications, fiber optics, high-speed interconnects, semiconductors, networking hardware, data-center infrastructure, or advanced hardware manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated experience sourcing fiber-optic components, optical cable assemblies, sourcing fiber connectivity, passive optical assemblies, optical packaging/assembly services, or similar high-volume hardware-integration categories.Strong familiarity with the fiber and optical interconnect supply chain, including cable assemblies, harnesses, fiber shuffles, backplanes, FAUs, fiber-to-chip interfaces,optical packaging services.electronics, assembly, test, and associated manufacturing processes.

 - Experience evaluating optical and interconnect suppliers against technical requirements such as bandwidth, insertion loss, signal integrity, reliability, thermal performance, power, quality, manufacturability, and production readiness.

 - Understanding of the technical and supply-chain challenges associated with scaling high-speed optical connectivity in AI, hyperscale data-center, or high-performance computing environments.

 - A proven track record of leading competitive sourcing processes, negotiating complex commercial agreements, and building long-term supplier partnerships.

 - Expertise in should-cost modeling, open-book pricing, total cost of ownership, supplier cost structures, and commercial optimization for hardware components and assemblies.

 - Experience securing supplier capacity and managing supply constraints across complex, multi-tier global supply chains.

 - Experience supporting supplier qualification, product development, manufacturing readiness, program bring-up, production ramp, and ongoing supplier performance management.

 - The technical credibility to collaborate effectively with optical, electrical, signal-integrity, systems, manufacturing, and reliability engineers and translate engineering requirements into actionable sourcing strategies.

 - Strong analytical judgment and the ability to balance cost, performance, supply continuity, quality, capacity, and delivery across a complex supplier ecosystem.

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager, SMB Ads
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to build, own, and lead lifecycle programs for SMB advertisers at OpenAI. This is a zero-to-one opportunity to establish the strategy and programs that guide businesses from initial interest and their first campaign to sustained success and growth.

You will set the lifecycle strategy, own the program roadmap and performance goals, and lead delivery from customer insight and journey design through launch, measurement, and iteration. Combining behavioral insights, experimentation, and personalized engagement across email, product experiences, education, and other channels, you will build programs that scale with the business. Success requires independent judgment, analytical depth, cross-functional leadership, and hands-on execution.

In This Role, You Will

 - Own the lifecycle program portfolio across prospect conversion, activation, retention, repeat spend, reactivation, and expansion.

 - Map advertiser journeys using cohort analysis, product behavior, campaign performance, and customer feedback to identify high-impact growth opportunities.

 - Build segmented, triggered journeys that connect advertiser needs, intent, readiness, and behavior to relevant messages and next steps.

 - Lead prospect nurture and email acquisition programs. Coordinate audiences, retargeting, and conversion experiences with Growth Marketing.

 - Launch onboarding and education programs that help advertisers create campaigns, understand performance, adopt capabilities, and grow their investment.

 - Coordinate delivery across email, in-product and onsite experiences, retargeting, education, and sales engagement with channel and product teams.

 - Test audiences, messaging, channels, timing, frequency, and offers. Use holdouts and downstream results to measure incremental customer impact.

 - Define data signals, segmentation, instrumentation, automation, and measurement with Data Science, Marketing Operations, prospect intelligence teams, and Ads Engineering.

 - Maintain high standards for journey quality, contact frequency, suppression, consent, and deliverability with operations and privacy partners.

 - Improve activation, time to first campaign, retention, repeat spend, reactivation, and expansion. Scale effective programs and use AI to accelerate content, personalization, and analysis.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

 - Demonstrate a track record of building and leading lifecycle programs from strategy through execution, with measurable activation, retention, or customer-growth results.

 - Translate customer behavior into effective engagement strategies through customer empathy, clear communication, and disciplined prioritization.

 - Build behavioral segmentation and triggered programs using product and customer signals across multiple channels.

 - Apply cohort analysis, funnel diagnostics, retention measurement, and experimental design to distinguish engagement from incremental customer outcomes.

 - Bring hands-on experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms, such as Marketo or comparable tools, including journey logic, personalization, and quality assurance.

 - Lead cross-functional programs with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Sales, and Marketing Operations, aligning priorities and driving delivery.

 - Set strategy and launch programs in fast-moving environments while establishing repeatable processes and reliable measurement.

 - Bring experience with SMBs, self-serve products, advertising, SaaS, marketplaces, fintech, or other high-volume customer journeys. Use AI thoughtfully to improve personalization and execution.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience building lifecycle programs for SMB advertisers or self-serve advertising platforms.

 - Track record launching onboarding and education programs that accelerate first campaign creation and repeat spend.

 - Experience connecting email, in-product messaging, retargeting, and sales engagement into coordinated customer journeys.

 - Experience using holdout tests and cohort analysis to measure incremental retention and revenue impact.

 - Hands-on experience establishing behavioral triggers, automation, and measurement for new lifecycle programs.

 - Experience applying AI to improve personalization, content development, and campaign analysis.

Workplace & Location

 - San Francisco, CA. This role requires a hybrid schedule with an in office requirement from Monday - Wednesday.

OpenAI's Compensation team plays a crucial role in rewarding and retaining world-class talent who will ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. By crafting and implementing innovative compensation strategies, we ensure our compensation offerings are competitive, equitable, and aligned with OpenAI's mission to scale intelligently and ethically.

We are expanding our Compensation team and seeking a Compensation Business Partner to help build the compensation pillar for our go-to-market organization. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for someone who brings deep GTM compensation expertise and enjoys turning evolving business needs into practical, scalable programs.

As a member of the total rewards team, you will partner closely with GTM leaders, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, Finance, and other cross-functional teams. You will spearhead compensation work across benchmarking, offer review, program design, and job architecture, with particular focus on the needs of a rapidly growing commercial organization.

The shape of the work will evolve as the business grows. At times, you may independently lead key initiatives from strategy through execution. At other times, you will work alongside additional compensation partners and cross-functional resources. Success in this role requires comfort operating with ambiguity, strong judgment, and a willingness to stay close to the details while building for scale.

This is an individual contributor role, designed for a subject-matter expert and hands-on builder.

 - Build and evolve compensation programs that support OpenAI’s growing GTM organization.

 - Serve as a trusted compensation advisor to GTM leaders, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, and Finance.

 - Lead compensation analysis and approval for offers, balancing market context, internal consistency, and OpenAI’s compensation philosophy.

 - Own benchmarking and market analysis for GTM roles, translating insights into clear recommendations and scalable practices.

 - Partner on the design and optimization of sales compensation programs, job architecture, and related compensation frameworks.

 - Develop approaches that can flex with changing business priorities, organizational growth, and new talent needs.

 - Move fluidly between strategic design and hands-on execution, including building processes and operating mechanisms where they do not yet exist.

 - Collaborate with the broader Compensation team to share insights and strengthen company-wide programs.

 - 6+ years of compensation experience, including meaningful depth supporting GTM or commercial organizations.

 - A builder mindset: you are energized by ambiguity and comfortable creating structure as the business evolves.

jobs.title: GRC Technical Program Manager, Product Lifecycle Assurance
jobs.description:
About the Team

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) is foundational to Security delivering mission outcomes at OpenAI. The GRC team provides security assurances and builds compliance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but operational in how we do our work, and we partner deeply with Product, Security, Legal, Privacy, GTM, and Field Security to help OpenAI move quickly while maintaining trust with customers, auditors, regulators, and the public.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Product Lifecycle Assurance IC to help scale OpenAI’s GRC function across our product stack to ensure products address customer and regulatory compliance requirements at launch and regressions are detected promptly and corrected.

You will partner closely with Product, Security, Legal, and Privacy teams to make sure OpenAI can move quickly while maintaining our security, privacy and compliance claims and giving customers, auditors, and regulators assurance about how OpenAI handles user data. You are responsible for product assurance end-to-end from inception to post-launch (continuous) monitoring. You leverage existing workflows, reviews, and data and enhance, augment and build the components needed to create an end-to-end product assurance program.

This role is not about supporting SOC or ISO audits; it's a highly cross-functional and deeply technical operations role to ensure that OAI products meet the compliance bar at launch, regressions are prevented and detected, and our compliance state can be evidenced. This role also helps ensure that our product launch governance program operates effectively across key safety, privacy, legal and security stakeholders and lessons-learned from incidents and regressions are used to improve the program.

You or in partnership with engineering teams, build key controls in our infrastructure stack, developer workflows and launch tooling to provide developers with guardrails, perform CI/CD conformance checks, and  surface launches that need GRC guidance. You ensure that teams have the information needed to design and launch safety and meet them where they are. You exercise sound judgement in making high-stakes decisions related to product launch risk and controls.

You are comfortable working in high velocity, low friction development environments. Your work goes across team boundaries and you assist and enable other teams to realize product assurance objectives. You should be comfortable with complex (Kubernetes) system architectures and dataflows, working with engineering teams to understand what could go wrong and where and how controls should be applied. You should be comfortable working with Privacy engineering and Data Science to understand data maps and database schemas and leverage existing processes and controls to further product assurance goals.



We’re looking for people who bring:



 - Strong technical product lifecycle assurance and security and privacy compliance experience working in high velocity, low friction development environments.

 - Experience building technical controls, metrics, monitoring tools, CI/CD tooling, high-fidelity risk signals and dashboards to meet product assurance goals

 - Ability to run an end-to-end, cross-functional, product assurance program applying judgement where what type of process or controls should be in place to meet a high assurance bar

 - Capacity to shift product assurance to the left in the product development cycle with just-in-time controls, guidance, guardrails and responsible friction for developers

 - Low ego outcome oriented mindset to achieve the product assurance goal required for OAI’s mission

 - Strong technical cross-functional leadership and don’t work in a vacuum - they influence, align and direct partner teams to achieve product assurance goals.

 - Exercise sound judgement in making high-stakes decisions related to product launch risk and controls.

You’ll be responsible for:

 - The end-to-end effective operation of OAI’s product assurance program from product development to post-launch (continuous) monitoring

 - Owning the GRC product assurance program, providing governance over Safety, Deployment, Security, Legal reviews to ensure we effectively surface product risk and design scalable mitigations

 - Driving cross-function collaboration and accountability in all aspects of the product assurance program

 - Building controls and low-friction, scalable processes in our infrastructure stack, developer workflows and launch tooling to ensure effective product assurance

 - Ensuring that teams have the guidance needed to design and launch safety and meet them where they are

 - Ensuring compliance, security and privacy claims and maps to verifiable controls

 - Recognizing how the product lifecycle assurance program fits into the large organizational objectives and when to build and when to influence and maintain strong partnerships with partner teams and influence roadmaps to further assurance goals

 - Applying sound judgement in launch reviews, technical assurance trade-off and management of OAI risk posture to guide product and engineering teams on the highest priorities

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Manager - Web & Organic, SMB Ads
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a Growth Marketing Manager to build the web and organic growth engine for SMB advertisers at OpenAI. This is a zero-to-one opportunity to shape how businesses discover our advertising platform, understand its value, and become successful advertisers.

You will own the SMB Ads web strategy and experimentation roadmap, combining customer insight, analytical rigor, and product judgment to grow qualified discovery and improve conversion. Your scope spans web experiences, organic search, generative engine optimization (GEO), and the journey from first visit through signup and activation. You will work closely with Product, Design, Ads Engineering, Content, and Data Science to turn opportunities into shipped experiences, operating with the speed and ownership of a startup.

In This Role, You Will

 - Own the SMB Ads web strategy and roadmap to grow qualified discovery, signup, and advertiser activation.

 - Grow organic discovery through search, content, and GEO. Test new ways to help businesses find and evaluate OpenAI’s advertising offering.

 - Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to identify conversion barriers and prioritize high-impact improvements.

 - Run experiments across landing pages, messaging, navigation, personalization, offers, and conversion flows. Use results to guide the roadmap.

 - Improve the journey from website visit to signup, onboarding, and first campaign with Product and Ads Engineering.

 - Define instrumentation, test design, attribution, and reporting with Data Science and marketing systems teams to measure incremental activation and advertiser value.

 - Launch useful web experiences with Content, Product Marketing, Design, Engineering, and specialist agencies. Evaluate capabilities such as personalization, chat, and experimentation tools.

 - Connect landing experiences to in-product, referral, and cross-sell acquisition programs. Coordinate onboarding and engagement with Lifecycle Marketing.

 - Use AI to accelerate research, prototyping, content, analysis, and experimentation. Scale successful tests and communicate results clearly.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

 - Bring 4–7 years of experience in growth marketing, web strategy, organic acquisition, conversion optimization, or product growth, with measurable acquisition, activation, or revenue impact.

 - Apply strong analytical judgment across funnels, cohorts, customer behavior, and incremental impact to prioritize growth opportunities.

 - Demonstrate ownership of web experiences and experimentation programs that improve conversion from discovery to activation.

 - Connect SEO, content-led discovery, and GEO with customer insight, web strategy, and product judgment.

 - Translate business opportunities into clear roadmaps and launched experiences with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing.

 - Combine strategic thinking with hands-on growth execution. Relevant backgrounds include scaled technology businesses, startups, or consulting followed by operating experience in startup growth.

 - Evaluate and implement web capabilities with technical partners, using AI to improve execution speed and quality.

 - Understand SMB customers and bring experience in self-serve products, advertising, SaaS, marketplaces, fintech, commerce, or other high-volume digital businesses.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience building web and organic growth programs for SMBs or self-serve advertising platforms.

 - Track record improving conversion from website discovery through signup and first campaign activation.

 - Experience growing qualified traffic through SEO, content, and generative engine optimization (GEO).

 - Hands-on experience testing landing pages, personalization, and onboarding flows to drive incremental growth.

 - Experience implementing web instrumentation, attribution, and experimentation tools with technical partners.

 - Experience using AI to accelerate research, prototyping, content development, and analysis

Workplace & Location

 - San Francisco, CA. This role requires a hybrid schedule with an in office requirement from Monday - Wednesday.

jobs.description:
About the Team

The Integrated Marketing team sits at the center of product, brand, creative, media, research, and GTM work. We partner closely with PMM, Product, Developer Relations, Design, Comms, and agency teams to shape launches and campaigns that are clear, distinctive, and grounded in real audience insight. This is a growing function, so the team needs people who can both raise the quality of the work and build the operating model around it: bringing strong judgment, high agency, and trusted partnership to complex, visible moments.



About the Role

OpenAI business launches move quickly and often involve new products, model capabilities, or research that can change how businesses operate.

We’re looking for an integrated marketing manager to help shape those launches from early strategy through execution. You’ll develop a point of view on the audience, positioning, creative direction, and channels, and help turn complex product and research advances into campaigns that connect with customers.

You’ll partner across Product, Product Marketing, Research, Brand, Creative, Communications, Growth, and Sales, along with external agencies. The right person understands technology, has strong strategic and creative instincts, and knows how to bring together the right people and ideas to produce work that is clear, credible, and effective.

This is a hybrid role based in San Francisco, with three days a week in the office.



In this role, you will:

 - Develop integrated marketing strategies for business product launches, new capabilities, model releases, and research moments.

 - Partner with Product, Product Marketing, and Research to understand what’s changing, identify the right audiences, and shape positioning and launch narratives.

 - Lead campaigns that bring launches to life across creative, communications, customer marketing, developer marketing, growth, sales, and paid, owned, and earned channels.

 - Identify customer stories, product demonstrations, and creative concepts that make technical capabilities tangible and relevant to business audiences.

 - Work with creative, media, and production agencies to develop briefs, evaluate ideas, and deliver strong campaigns.

 - Connect launch strategies to the needs of customers, sales teams, and partners, making sure the work supports both immediate announcements and longer-term adoption.

 - Manage campaign budgets, agency relationships, and media investments where appropriate.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have ~10+ years of experience in B2B product marketing, integrated marketing, launches, and/or a related technology go-to-market role. We care more about the scope, quality, and complexity of your work than an exact number of years.

 - Have launched enterprise software, AI products, cloud services, developer tools, or other technically sophisticated offerings, especially in fast moving or ambiguous environments.

 - Understand product positioning and can work closely with Product and PMM leaders as a thoughtful, credible partner.

We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Sales, Partnerships, Marketing Operations, Design, and Communications to create a cohesive end-to-end advertiser experience and help businesses unlock value from OpenAI's advertising platform.

We are hiring a Growth Marketing Manager, SMB Ads to help build and execute high-velocity growth programs for small business advertisers. This person will work across acquisition, activation, lifecycle, and conversion, with an initial focus on helping advertisers move from interest and sign-up to first meaningful spend & retention over time

This is a hands-on growth role for someone who loves turning ideas into shipped experiments. You will build campaigns, lifecycle journeys, landing page tests, messaging tests, audience experiments, AI-assisted workflows, reporting improvements, and practical conversion programs. As the SMB Ads business grows, this role may continue to support acquisition and activation and expand deeper into same-store growth, lifecycle, retention, and repeat spend.

 - Execute growth experiments across acquisition, activation, lifecycle, and early retention.
